evidence: From the signposted car park at the east end of the Cass River road bridge, follow the vehicle track next to the row of pine trees until it meets Cass River.
The track descends through beech and exotic forest to Bealey Hut (six bunks).
A further 5 minute walk from the hut takes you to the car park by Cora Lynn Station, and another 2 minutes to SH73.
Most trampers prefer to begin the track from the Cass end, as this avoids the steepest ascents.

doubts: Start taken as F2 (unnamed track meeting West Coast Road, i.e. SH73 at Cass) and end as F1 (unnamed track meeting Cora Lynn Road by Bealey Hut); the text says the end car park is 2 minutes from SH73 and is reached through the gate on Cora Lynn Road. The page notes the route can be walked in reverse from the Cora Lynn Road end, recorded as an access point rather than a separate way. The Long Creek ref T14 marks the creek, used for its confluence with the Harper River. No overall distance is given. Lagoon Saddle Shelter has no matching entry.
